title: Product PRD: Unified Inference — Pricing, Packaging & Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Consolidated product requirements, design notes, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted, dedicated, and private). Targets FY28 Q4 release and packaging refresh.
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the Product Requirements Document (PRD), high-level design specs, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family. It covers hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private variants with a focus on predictable economics, composable rollout, and observability-first shipping.

Goals:
- Deliver a single, consistent developer surface for text, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Reduce customer unit cost by 15% for typical web-search/assistant workloads through batching and caching recommendations.
- Provide clear packaging tiers for SMB, Mid-market, and Enterprise with predictable SLAs and upgrade paths.
- Launch FY28 Q4 with updated pricing and trial bundles.

Key features (vX.3 release):
- Streaming + function-calling parity across hosted and dedicated.
- Auto-quantization profiles and per-workload kernel selection.
- Route policies: latency-first, cost-first, and compliance pinned.
- Console: new cost breakdowns by route and token bucket.

Product requirements (priority ordered):
1) Developer surface: stable REST + SDK parity (Node/Python/Go). SLO: 99.9% API availability for hosted.
2) Cost controls: Batching policy UI; recommended cache TTL presets.
3) Dedicated capacity: SLA-backed latency targets (p50 < 50ms for 2k tokens, p95 < 200ms).
4) Private: offline packaging + KMS integration; upgrade path with zero-downtime agent.
5) Observability: per-route token-level cost, anomaly alerting, and regression hooks.

Requirements table (ID | Requirement | Owner | Acceptance criteria):
| ID | Requirement | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| R-101 | REST/SDK parity | DX | All public endpoints tested e2e; SDKs in GA |
| R-102 | Autoscaling policies | Eng-SRE | Configurable rules + load tests show <10% error at 2x nominal load |
| R-103 | Quant profiles | Eng-Serving | 2 quant profiles validated for 70B models with <2% quality delta |
| R-104 | Pricing tiers | Product | Pricing page and billing API support 3 tiers + add-ons |

Design notes (high level):
- Architecture: single control plane with pluggable runtime adapters. Runtime selects kernels by model shape and device capability.
- Data plane: requests routed to pools based on policy; prefix caching handled at the edge dispatcher.
- Packaging: containerized on-prem agent with an optional air-gapped installer; private control plane uses mTLS and customer KMS.

Examples:
- Sample call (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"rw-unified-70b","input":"Summarize..."}'

Roadmap & themes (Q4 FY28 -> Q2 FY29):
- FY28 Q4: Launch vX.3 (pricing refresh, new console cost breakdowns, Dedicated SLA).
- FY29 Q1: Private VPC GA, on-prem installer improvements, enterprise compliance pack.
- FY29 Q2: Model composition & reranking toolkit, quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.

Pricing & packaging guidance (principles):
- Three core tiers: Developer (freemium), Business (usage + modest commit), Enterprise (reserved capacity + support).
- Pricing levers: per-token generation, per-embedding measurement, and reserved GPU-hour credits for Dedicated.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance/evidence, SSO & SCIM integrations.
- Intro bundle (trial): 60 days free, $2000 credit for Dedicated POC, 10k free embedding units.

Sample pricing matrix (simplified):
| Tier | Billing model | Base SLA | Included credits |
| Developer | pay-as-you-go | best-effort | free trial credits |
| Business | monthly usage | 99.9% | 50k token credits |
| Enterprise | reserved + usage | 99.95% + 24x7 support | negotiable |

Release notes (vX.3, targeted 2028-11-30):
- Features: cost breakdowns per route, new batching policy UI, quantization profile v2, Dedicated SLA improvements.
- Bug fixes: SDK request timeout fixes, improved backpressure handling in dispatcher.
- Known issues: Private on-prem upgrade may require manual certificate rotation for clusters older than 2028-06. Workaround documented in eng-private-deployments.

Rollout & launch plan:
1) Canary: 2% traffic, monitoring for error rate and latency regressions for 72 hours.
2) Gradual ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days if no regressions.
3) Sales enablement: updated playbooks, pricing calculator, and battlecards two days before GA.
4) Customer migration: opt-in auto-migrate for Business tier customers; manual assistance for Enterprise.

SLOs & metrics to track:
- API availability: 99.9% (hosted).
- P50 latency: <50ms for 2k tokens on Dedicated.
- Token cost reduction: target -15% vs baseline within 90 days.
- Regression alerts: triggered when quality metric delta >2% on control prompts.

2) Share migration guide and billing impact worksheet.
3) Offer Dedicated POC credits and 1:1 onboarding for Enterprise.
